events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph.** Expected boat rating: **2 (average)**.
- **Fish deep, 120 feet or more.** The latest St. Joseph boat reports had fish well past 120 feet of water.
- **Expected ratings for the others:** South Haven **1 (below average)**, Grand Haven **1**, Muskegon **0-1** (low confidence, since it has no recent boat salmon report).
- **Lures:** spoons were the most-cited producer. Shrimp did well at St. Joseph in late June.

## Why

- **St. Joseph is the best recent boat option:** the July 5 St. Joseph report rated boat salmon fishing average, the best of the four ports that week (St. Joseph, 2023-07-05).
- **Deep water is where the fish were:** the July 5 reports had boats fishing beyond 120 feet at St. Joseph and about 100 feet at South Haven (St. Joseph, 2023-07-05; South Haven, 2023-07-05).
- **Past summers at similar water temperatures were mostly slow:** I'd expect this week to be average at best, because similar-temperature weeks in earlier seasons were rated 0-2, with most at 0-1.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is 13 days old, except Grand Haven and Muskegon)**
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-05: boat fishing "decent," quality 2, "well beyond 120 feet of water," mixed bag.
- South Haven, 2023-07-05: "fair," quality 1, boats "fishing very deep water," a few fish near 100 feet, most caught on spoons.
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21 (27 days old): quality 2, fish 35-90 feet down in 65-160 feet of water, orange spoons and green or yellow meat rigs.
- Muskegon: no boat salmon report in the last four weeks. Its latest report is from June 7, 41 days old.

**Past seasons (similar surface temperature, same time of year)**
- Grand Haven, 2022-07-14: quality 0, slow; fish 45-120 feet down in 100-180 feet of water.
- Muskegon, 2022-07-14: quality 0, slow; best action 45-100 feet down in 100-200 feet of water.
- St. Joseph, 2022-07-06: quality 1; best water 30-40 feet, though most fish were deeper than 100 feet.
- South Haven, 2022-07-06: quality 0, slow; best water well beyond 100 feet.
- St. Joseph, 2022-06-29: quality 2, rotators, flies and spoons, fish beyond 100 feet.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water (measured): St. Joseph 71 F (flat over the week), South Haven 71 F (+2 F), Grand Haven 68 F (+4 F), Muskegon 68 F (+4 F) (buoy summaries, 2023-07-18).
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before today, not live data. It included no cold-layer depth model and no wind forecast.

## Caveats

- **Report age:** the St. Joseph and South Haven reports are 13 days old. Grand Haven's is 27 days old, and Muskegon's has no recent boat salmon data. Treat these as a guide.
- **Water temperature:** the buoy surface is measured, but the modeled cold-layer depth and wind forecast were not available, so I can't say where the 52-58 F water is this week.
- **General guidance (NY DEC, Michigan Sea Grant):** Chinook and coho prefer 52-58 F water, and the thermocline in summer can be a narrow band. The warm surface near 70 F suggests salmon are deep, but that is my inference, not a report finding.
- **Wind:** check the forecast before going. Small-boat safety comes first, and the pier or river is the fallback if waves are high.

## Sources

- St. Joseph and South Haven, July 5 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- St. Joseph, South Haven and Grand Haven, June 21 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- Past-season analogs: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31f444a, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31e454b, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf
